title: Ohè, là, le guardie!
subtitle: Dawn in the snow at the Barrière d'Enfer: street sweepers, the tavern song with Musetta, milkmaids, carters and peasant women at the toll gate, La bohème, Act 3

passages.label: Prelude: snow falling at dawn at the Barrière d'Enfer (Andantino mosso)
Ohè, là, le guardie! The street sweepers at the gate; the customs officer: Vengo!
From the tavern: Chi nel ber trovò il piacer, and Musetta's song (D major)
Trallerallè (the men in the tavern, Poco più mosso); milkmaids and carters at the gate
Burro e cacio! The peasant women pass through the gate and go their ways

licences.author: Luigi Illica (1857–1919) and Giuseppe Giacosa (1847–1906)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Ricordi vocal score.

licences.source: G. Ricordi & C. vocal score of La bohème, pages 167-176 (from the start of Act 3, page 167, to the end of page 176 system 3, before figure (6), 174 bars)
licences.author: Carlo Carignani (1857–1919), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: sung lines and piano each transcribed independently, disagreements settled on the page by a separate judge, then checked against the print and corrected. The print's chorus groups (street sweepers; three-part women's and three men's staves in the tavern; milkmaids; carters; two groups of peasant women) are gathered here into three staves by voice (every note kept, each group named where it comes in; parts printed together on one staff, or with the same words and rhythm, are written as chords; the two groups of peasant women are written as separate voices on the staff where they sing in the same bar). Shouted notes printed without noteheads are written with x noteheads. Tempo from the printed metronome mark (Andantino mosso ♩ = 112) and the printed a tempo; the Poco più mosso is a value chosen as stated in the piece's notes.
